scenarios.scenario: CREDIT MINTED WITHOUT A GRAPH WRITE. An attacker (or ordinary traffic) drives a resolve that reaches the accrual hook while the cross-tenant graph write silently no-ops. The site is paid a credit for data it never contributed, inflating the money surface. Four distinct no-op paths exist: missing fingerprint, missing email, visitor.do_not_resolve set, and an email tombstoned under GRAPH_WRITE_BLOCKING_SCOPES ('erased', 'do_not_process') or 'all'. A fifth path is a write that raises and rolls back.
scenarios.mechanism: _upsert_beam_identity was changed from `-> None` to `-> bool` and returns True at exactly ONE place — immediately after `await self.db.commit()` succeeds (identity_resolver.py:1332). Every other exit returns False: the fingerprint/email guard (1275), the combined do_not_resolve/suppression erasure guard (1289), and the except path (1336, which previously fell through to an implicit None). The hook is `if wrote_graph and settings.identity_coop_enabled:` — a short-circuit on the return value, so no no-op path can reach record_contribution at all. This was FAIL F2 in the 2nd outer-PVL pass and is the single most important guard in the phase.
provingTests: tests/unit/test_identity_coop.py::test_upsert_returns_bool_and_existing_callers_unaffected (True only on committed write; False on a raising write)
scenarios.nonVacuity: Against the pre-change code these tests are genuinely RED: `_upsert_beam_identity` returned None, so `assert wrote is False` fails (None is not False) and `assert ... is True` fails. The assertions are identity checks on the exact value, not truthiness, so they cannot pass against the old implementation.
scenarios.residual: A future editor could add a new early-return to _upsert_beam_identity and forget `False`. Mitigation: the function's docstring states the contract explicitly, and test_blocked_graph_write_accrues_nothing parametrizes per path so a new unguarded path is likely to surface. Not fully mechanical — accepted.

scenarios.scenario: ERASED-PERSON ROW CREATION. A person exercises GDPR erasure; SPEC A's sweep deletes their beam_identity_graph rows. They later visit any Beam site. The co-op writes a NEW identity_contribution_events row bearing their email_bidx. Because ERASURE_TARGETS = ('beam_identity_graph',) does not include the co-op tables, that row is unreachable by the sweep — a fresh record of a person created AFTER their erasure, permanently. This is a privacy defect, not a bookkeeping one.
scenarios.mechanism: Two independent layers. (1) The erasure guard inside _upsert_beam_identity returns False for anyone tombstoned under GRAPH_WRITE_BLOCKING_SCOPES or 'all', so the hook never fires — NOTHING is written, not even an excluded_reason='erased' audit row (decision D-B chose 'write nothing' over 'write an excluded row', precisely because an excluded row still carries the email_bidx). (2) identity_coop.py imports no suppression symbol and re-lists no scope literal, so there is no second, drifting copy of the scope list that could go narrower than the resolver's — the exact defect class (erased-only narrowness) found as C1. ERASURE_TARGETS and the sweep are untouched by this phase.
provingTests: tests/unit/test_identity_coop.py::test_erased_person_leaves_no_new_bidx_row (asserts wrote is False AND no email_bidx-bearing write occurred)
tests/unit/test_identity_coop.py::test_coop_module_imports_no_suppression_scope (AST-based tripwire: no suppression import, no 'erased'/'do_not_process'/'all' string literal in executable code)
scenarios.nonVacuity: test_erased_person_leaves_no_new_bidx_row patches is_email_suppressed_any to return True and asserts the record_contribution mock is NEVER awaited (it is armed with side_effect=AssertionError). If the guard were removed the mock fires and the test fails loudly. The tripwire test is AST-based rather than substring-based specifically so it cannot be satisfied vacuously by the module's own docstring naming the forbidden symbols.
scenarios.residual: The invariant depends on the resolver's erasure guard remaining upstream of the hook. If a future edit moved the hook above that guard, ADV-2 reopens. The hook's position immediately after the _upsert_beam_identity call (and its dependence on that call's return) makes this structurally hard but not impossible.

scenarios.scenario: DAILY CREDIT INFLATION. The same person is resolved by the same site on many days. The per-day audit key (site_id, email_bidx, contributed_on) permits one row per day, so a naive implementation mints a fresh credit every calendar day forever for one identity — unbounded credit inflation from a single contribution.
scenarios.mechanism: A PARTIAL unique index uq_coop_accrued_site_email on (site_id, email_bidx) WHERE accrued IS TRUE (decision D-E). At most one ACCRUED row per identity per site, ever. The service reaches accrual by attempting the accrued=True UPDATE inside a SAVEPOINT and catching IntegrityError — so the DB, not application code, is the enforcement point and a concurrent double-resolve cannot slip through. Repeat resolves still record an audit row with excluded_reason='duplicate'.
provingTests: tests/integration/test_identity_coop_contribution.py::test_accrued_partial_unique_index_exists_and_blocks_second_credit (asserts the index exists WITH a WHERE predicate, then proves a raw SQL duplicate INSERT — bypassing ALL service code — is rejected by Postgres)
scenarios.nonVacuity: The integration leg asserts the index definition contains 'WHERE' — a non-partial unique index would pass a mere existence check but is the WRONG constraint (it would reject the later-day audit row the design keeps deliberately). The duplicate-insert leg uses raw psql-equivalent SQL, so service-code correctness cannot mask a missing index. Verified live against a disposable postgres:16-alpine: 'ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint uq_coop_accrued_site_email'.

scenarios.scenario: VACUOUS CONSENT. A client flips contribution_enabled=True while sending terms_version="x" (or any junk), satisfying a presence-only guard. The site is enrolled in a cross-tenant data co-op with an audit trail that records acceptance of terms that never existed — the worst possible failure on a consent surface, because it looks compliant.
scenarios.mechanism: E4's validator: the router 422s unless terms_version is a 64-char lowercase hex string AND equals settings.coop_terms_version (the pinned sha256 of the exact policy text). record_consent_acceptance runs before the handler's single `await db.commit()`, so the acceptance row and the flag flip are one transaction — 'flag ON with no matching audit row' is not a reachable state. Opting OUT requires no acceptance, deliberately: gating withdrawal from a data co-op would itself be a consent defect.
provingTests: tests/integration/test_identity_coop_contribution.py::test_flag_on_requires_acceptance (5 legs: missing; wrong FORMAT "x"; right format but wrong value 'a'*64; the pinned version ⇒ 200 + exactly one row; opt-out unconditional and does not rewind the trail)
scenarios.nonVacuity: Leg 2 sends exactly the terms_version="x" the plan named as the vacuous-guard case; leg 3 sends a well-formed 64-hex string that is NOT the pinned digest, so a format-only validator passes leg 2 but FAILS leg 3. Each rejection leg re-reads the flag from the DB and asserts it is still False, so a 422 that nevertheless persisted the flip would be caught.
scenarios.residual: This is a constant compare against a single pinned version. It cannot express multi-version history or migration between terms versions — Phase 3's coop_terms.py owns that and supersedes this check. Accepted and documented in the config comment.

scenarios.scenario: PII LEAK VIA THE CO-OP TABLES. The new tables or their logs expose plaintext email, or provide a decrypt path that turns the contribution log into a cross-tenant email directory.
scenarios.mechanism: identity_contribution_events stores email_bidx (an HMAC-SHA256 blind index from pii_crypto.email_hash) and has NO email and NO email_ciphertext column — so unlike beam_identity_graph there is no decrypt path out of these tables at all, by construction rather than by policy. The resolver computes the blind index before calling into the co-op module, so plaintext never crosses the boundary. structlog calls log site_id/reason/amount only; email_bidx is deliberately not logged either.
provingTests: tests/unit/test_identity_coop.py::test_contribution_event_carries_blind_index_only (asserts email_bidx present and {email, email_ciphertext} absent from the table)
tests/integration/test_identity_coop_contribution.py::test_qualifying_contribution_writes_ledger_row (asserts the persisted event's email_bidx equals the expected hash and contains no '@')
scenarios.nonVacuity: The column-absence assertion fails immediately if anyone adds an email or ciphertext column to the model.
scenarios.residual: email_bidx is a stable identity key: it cannot be reversed to an address, but it CAN correlate the same person across sites. That is inherent to the co-op's purpose (dedupe + attribution) and is what the opt-in flag and consent trail exist to govern. Not a defect; a disclosed property.

scenarios.scenario: CO-OP FAILURE BREAKS IDENTIFICATION. A bug or missing table in the co-op path raises and aborts _save_identified, so a paid, successful identification is lost — the co-op damaging the core product it is supposed to reward.
scenarios.mechanism: Two nested best-effort layers, matching the existing hot_alert precedent in the same function. record_contribution wraps its entire body in try/except with a rollback and a keys-only structlog.warning; maybe_record_contribution (the resolver-facing entrypoint) wraps its own site-lookup and translation in a second try/except. Neither can propagate.
provingTests: tests/unit/test_identity_coop.py::test_coop_failure_does_not_break_identification (every execute raises; asserts no ledger row and that rollback ran)
scenarios.nonVacuity: The fake session raises RuntimeError on every execute; without the try/except the test errors out rather than passing.
scenarios.residual: A swallowed failure means a genuine contribution silently goes uncredited. Accepted tradeoff: under-crediting is strictly safer than breaking a resolve or over-crediting, and the warning is logged for operator visibility.

scenarios.scenario: READ ACCESS QUIETLY GATED ON CONTRIBUTION. The co-op turns into pay-to-play: a site with contribution_enabled=False stops receiving graph-served identifications, breaking the locked AC-2 constraint (read is unconditional, model (a)) for every existing customer the moment the flag ships.
scenarios.mechanism: No gate was added to any read path. Enforced structurally rather than behaviourally: an AST assertion walks _graph_node_by_email and _check_beam_identity_network and asserts neither body references contribution_enabled or identity_coop. The 11-line resolver diff is confined to the WRITE path and the hook that follows it.
scenarios.nonVacuity: The AST check asserts absence in named read functions, so adding any co-op reference to either read path fails the test. A purely behavioural test could pass by luck on an unrelated code path; this cannot.
scenarios.residual: Only the two named graph-read functions are asserted. A future third read path would not be covered automatically.

scenarios.scenario: MIGRATION DAMAGE. The two new revisions rewrite or lock the high-traffic sites table, silently opt existing sites in, chain onto a stale head and fork the DAG, or cannot be reverted.
scenarios.mechanism: Both revisions are additive-only: three CREATE TABLE plus one ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN with server_default='false' (non-blocking on PG 11+, no table rewrite, every existing row backfilled OFF — no site is ever opted in by a migration). NOT NULL with a default rather than nullable, because 'unknown' must not be representable for a consent flag. The head was re-derived LIVE (`alembic heads` → d1a6c4e93f27, single head) immediately before writing, and both revisions chain onto it. Full round-trip proven on a disposable postgres:16-alpine.
provingTests: G2 live round-trip: upgrade head (66 revisions from empty) → downgrade -1 → downgrade -1 → upgrade head, clean both directions, final `current` = f2c81a6b4d09 (head)
A7 offline: alembic upgrade d1a6c4e93f27:head --sql exits 0
psql verification of the partial index definition and sites.contribution_enabled (NOT NULL, default false) after the round-trip
scenarios.nonVacuity: The round-trip ran against a real Postgres with a real 66-revision chain from an empty database, not an offline --sql dry run. The downgrade legs were verified to leave the head at d1a6c4e93f27 and the upgrade legs to restore the partial index.
scenarios.residual: NOT applied to any real environment. Live apply remains a separate explicit operator action, and the head must be re-derived again at that time — this repo's head moves on a roughly daily cadence.
